methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-institution analysis of 83 USC patients (2015-2023) with IHC-based molecular characterization (TP53, ER, PR, HER2, MMR status). Retrospectively reclassified by FIGO 2023 staging. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with log-rank testing and Cox regression for univariate/multivariable analysis. Limitations: retrospective single-center design, modest sample size, IHC for molecular assessment (not sequencing), missing/incomplete molecular data for some patients, no external validation cohort.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective case series (LoE 4) characterizing rare aggressive USC subtype. Identifies ER expression as prognostic marker for improved DFS but not PFS/OS. Clinical utility limited by lack of novel treatment targets; findings mainly confirm molecular heterogeneity without actionable therapeutic implications.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK-aligned prognostic biomarker study: patient selection criteria, baseline characteristics, molecular findings, survival analysis. IHC methodology described. Limitations: incomplete data for some biomarkers; no data repository statement.

novelty_literature.justification: Single-institution analysis of ER expression in USC; ER prognostic role in endometrial cancer established in other subtypes. Limited novelty as findings largely confirmatory of known ER associations.

writing_presentation.justification: Organized clinicopathological analysis with appropriate context for rare aggressive USC subtype. Methods and results clearly presented. Publication-ready structure.

key_strengths: Multi-institutional molecular characterization using FIGO 2023 risk stratification; ER expression identifies prognostically favorable DFS subset
Comprehensive IHC assessment including TP53, ER, PR, HER2, MMR status
Transparent acknowledgment of single-center retrospective design limitations
key_concerns: Single-center USC cohort (n=83) with modest sample size; no external validation
IHC-based molecular assessment rather than sequencing; missing/incomplete data for some patients
ER prognostic effect limited to DFS without PFS/OS benefit; limited clinical actionability
No novel treatment targets or therapeutic strategies identified; findings confirmatory
chief_reviewer.rationale: Descriptive single-center case series on rare USC with ER prognostic role for DFS, but small sample, single-center design, and lack of novel therapeutic insights limit tier to 4.
